context: Place four queens on a 4×4 chessboard so that no two share a row, column, or diagonal. The original boards have no coordinate labels. Here, rows are numbered from top to bottom and columns from left to right, starting at 1.
description: The table gives the queen’s column in each row of the left and right boards, from top to bottom. All other squares are empty.

frames.explanation: Each arrangement has one queen per row and column. For any two queens, the absolute difference between their row numbers differs from the absolute difference between their column numbers, so they share neither kind of diagonal. The arrangements are mirror images across the vertical axis and constitute all solutions.
frames.title: The two four-queen solutions

summary: The left and right boards show the two valid solutions to the 4-queens problem.
